text:
sana: flagging a recurring p95 wobble on eu-central rack c9 since 01:20 UTC. pattern: short ~30s spikes every ~6m, seems to coincide with tenant-fastapi starting heavy batched export jobs.

ctrl-bot: [ALERT] eu-central/rack-c9: p95 inference latency > 700ms for 7m (rule: infra.latency.p95)

viktor: grabbing metrics. any sign of NVLink/PCIe saturation or host egress?

mike: quick snapshot from 01:22:
```
2026-07-11T01:22:08Z rack=c9 host=eu-c9-07 gpu0 util=94 nvlink=84Gb/s nic_tx=3.9GB/s
2026-07-11T01:22:08Z rack=c9 host=eu-c9-07 gpu1 util=26 nvlink=9Gb/s nic_tx=0.1GB/s
2026-07-11T01:22:08Z rack=c9 host=eu-c9-08 gpu0 util=90 nvlink=79Gb/s nic_tx=3.6GB/s
```

aline: yup bimodal util and host tx spikes. tenant-fastapi's exporter opens many asynchronous streams and writes temp artifacts to shared NAS which spikes host IO and pushes NVLink arbitration.

sana: immediate mitigations? options: (a) soft-evict exporter replicas to ephemeral pool, (b) apply a per-tenant nvlink+nic cap, (c) temporarily schedule exporters to OFF-peak via cron marker. what has lowest risk?

viktor: (a) is fastest. we have ephemeral-eu with ~8% spare capacity. do a dry-run first for PDB impact.

mike: dry-run shows 6 exporter pods, 2 honor PDB. reschedule will move 4. I'll run:
```
apictl placement reschedule --rack c9 --label role=exporter --to-pool ephemeral-eu --grace 90s
```

ctrl-bot: user mike started placement reschedule (role=exporter) on rack c9

aline: also please add a temporary alert for NVLink asymmetry (gpu.util.stddev>0.24) so the fallback controller can abort before p95 hits.

sana: running reschedule now. watch p95 and nvlink metrics.

mike: reschedule in progress: 3/6 moved, 1 blocking on PDB, 2 in progress. p95 dropped to ~210ms after two moves. :thumbsup:

viktor: nice. long-term we should avoid placing exporters (heavy host IO) on racks with latency-sensitive pods and consider an explicit tag `io-intensive=true` for placement filters. also surface per-tenant nvlink and nic_tx in console.

aline: agree. I'll own a short RFC for placement-tagging + console metrics. sana: can you draft the incident blurb for #incidents? include action items: reschedule done, temp alert, RFC owner.

sana: will do. leaving the temp placement rule for 30m. if this recurs we'll evaluate carving tenant-fastapi into a small dedicated slice for predictable performance (cost estimate needed).

mike: FYI I'll prototype a scheduler pre-filter that rejects new placements where target racks report recent nvlink asymmetry. won't be immediate but should reduce repeat incidents.

ctrl-bot: reminder: please update incident once stabilized.

viktor: reschedule complete; p95 stable ~190ms for last 10m. closing loop after incident note posted. thanks team.
